mechanism_narrative: Because WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are still far below baseline but have been steadily improving from t-3w to t-1w, continued normalization should increase discretionary stops after commutes and lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue rising for two more weekly observations but RETAIL_REC does not improve relative to the last 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL remains elevated above +10% while TRANSIT stays below -30%, more activities are substituted to home-based consumption and nearby essentials, which depresses retail and recreation spending over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above +10% and TRANSIT stays below -30% but RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean within two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed drop in PARKS together with a downward reversal in TRANSIT signals tighter movement constraints or weaker outing propensity, which should spill over into lower retail and recreation visits within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 5 points week-on-week after a prior rise
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -6.4 to -24.1 while TRANSIT stayed near -37
failure_condition: If PARKS drops by more than 5 points week-on-week and TRANSIT also weakens, yet RETAIL_REC does not fall in the following week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GROCERY_PHARM from its near-baseline level indicates more errand traffic and neighborhood circulation, which should modestly pull RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks through spillover shopping trips.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains near or above baseline for four weeks but RETAIL_REC does not move upward relative to the prior four weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES remains below -25% and RESIDENTIAL stays above +13%, the city is operating in a stay-at-home pattern that reduces exposure to discretionary shopping opportunities, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES stays below -25% and RESIDENTIAL stays above +13% but RETAIL_REC improves over the next 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An isolated rebound in PARKS after a trough usually reflects weather- or holiday-driven outdoor substitution, which diverts trips away from malls and dining districts and lowers RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises at least 8 points from a recent low
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -21.3 to -6.4 before dropping again
failure_condition: If PARKS rebounds by at least 8 points from a recent low and RETAIL_REC fails to decline within two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT crosses upward through -35% while WORKPLACES is still improving, the combined easing of access and commuting should raise retail footfall with a lag of about four weeks.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses above -35% and WORKPLACES keeps improving, but RETAIL_REC is not higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a steady-state recovery, a plateau in WORKPLACES near -25% combined with no further improvement in TRANSIT means commuting gains have stalled, so the earlier retail rebound also stalls and RETAIL_REC drifts lower over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved only marginally from -25.7 to -24.9 while TRANSIT was flat near -37
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT flatten at roughly current levels but RETAIL_REC does not weaken within one week, the hypothesis is rejected.
